title: Report body (structured long-form document)
description: One long-form research report already flattened into render-ready blocks. THE FLATTENING IS THE CONTRACT: inline emphasis and links are resolved to text upstream of this shape, so `text` carries no markup and a consumer must not re-parse it as HTML. The parse is guarded by a MEASURED floor rather than a guess: a body shorter than the layout-drift floor is not treated as a short report but as a changed page and becomes a loud error, because an empty or partial upstream is never a valid answer. `published_at` follows the same rule as news: absent on the list variant (the homepage source publishes no dates) and present only when the report page itself was fetched.

slug.description: The report's own slug - the only key this provider model has (it is echoed from the request on keyed modes).

published_at.description: Null on the list variant BY DESIGN (no date is published there) - render an em-dash, never a date and never 0.

authors.description: Null when the byline is ambiguous: the parser refuses to guess an author rather than attributing the piece to the wrong person.

sections.description: Document-order headings, used as the reader view's table of contents.

type.description: The block's own semantic level, taken from the document.

text.description: Render-ready plain text; inline markup has ALREADY been flattened, so this must never be injected as HTML.
